newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary BUX firms in slack trade, futures edge up.
newsitem.headline: Hungary BUX firms in slack trade, futures edge up.

text.p: The Budapest Stock Exchange drifted higher on Tuesday benefiting from a stronger dollar but traders said the market's rising trend was not yet convincing enough as many investors remained inactive.
The BUX index finished at 5,595.62 points, up 35.36, but with a hardly more than half percent gain it lagged behind some massively rising European markets.
BUX futures advanced for all maturities by between 0.50 to 43.50 points. March futures closed at 5,690 points, up 15.

"The market continued to rise...because the dollar regained its power," said Peter Nagy of Postabank Securities. However, he said, the fact that many stocks closed below their daily peaks suggested that the rising trend was not strong enough.
Hotel firm Danubius, OTP Bank and TVK all closed higher, but below their daily highs.
Danubius outperformed most other rising stocks on Tuesday as it closed at 5,650 forints, up 235 from Monday, but below the day's peak of 5,750.

"The share fell to levels (in the past few days) which triggered new purchases, mainly from domestic clients," one trader said earlier today. Another said that Danubius rose on the back of speculative purchases by domestic small investors.
Daily spot share turnover totalled 2.05 billion forints which is not particularly strong compared to some of the most active days in January and earlier this month.

"This two billion (forints) of turnover is very low compared to four billion to five billion forints earlier," Nagy said. "Foreign investors are less active than before...they sit on their stocks and wait."
One target of their expectations was the next phase of a share issue in oil and gas company MOL.

Traders said there was good demand for shares in plastics company Pannonplast and home improvement product maker Graboplast even though the latter one closed lower. Graboplast ended at 8,500 forints, down 90, while Pannonplast edged up 20 forints to 7,900.
On the negative territory, Egis dropped nearly five percent on foreigners' sales and closed at 10,850 forints, down 500.

Traders said earlier today they were not aware of any fresh developments around Egis, but late last Thursday ABN-AMRO Hoare Govett gave a 'sell' recommendation on the stock, triggered by the 1996 preliminary results.
